newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end lower, led by Bavaria.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end lower, led by Bavaria.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed down in sluggish trade on Monday, with brewer Bavaria, the flagship of the Julio Santo Domingo industrial empire, leading the decline.

Bogota's IBB index fell 0.34 percent to 1195.24 on trading of shares worth 1.7 billion pesos. Medellin's IBOMED .IBMG general price index dropped 0.54 percent to 18131.33 with shares worth 1 billion pesos changing hands.
"There was no spark in the market today...If the markets depend on foreign funds to move them and the funds don't move to buy, then you get days like today," one Bogota broker said.
Bavaria fell 0.31 percent to 7,925 in Bogota and 0.7 percent in Medellin to 7,924.

A cross-deal involving shares of Suramericana de Seguros, the insurance company that leads the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial conglomerate, accounted for much of the volume in Bogota. The stock was unchanged at 28,200 on trading of shares worth 564 million pesos.
In Medellin, Banco Industrial Colombiano fell 0.41 percent to 3,634.99.
